projectSummary: Within-participant acute surface-EMG comparison of four bench angles (0, 30, 45 and -15 degrees) at 65 per cent of one-repetition maximum in 14 resistance-trained males, with each contraction phase subdivided into four 25 per cent contraction-duration windows.

publication.statusSource: NCBI PubMed record fetched 2026-09-13; no retraction or correction notice

notes: Abstract only. The acquisition ladder was run in full on 2026-09-13 and returned no lawful full text; the publisher is closed to this client and no repository or PMC copy exists.

The headline result is a partial null: no upper-pectoralis difference across any bench condition over the complete concentric contraction, with differences appearing only in the 26 to 50 per cent contraction-duration window. A whole-contraction null and a sub-phase difference are different findings and must not be reported interchangeably.
This record is the second of the two studies R1 finding I-13 identified as absent from the first pass. It entered screening here through the amended portion-terminology stratum N-RS4a.
Surface EMG is an acute activation measure and is not evidence of hypertrophy.

study.population: Fourteen healthy resistance-trained males (age 21.4 (SD 0.4) years) performed one set of six repetitions of a free-weight barbell bench press at 0, 30, 45 and -15 degree bench angles at 65 per cent of one-repetition maximum.

title: Influence of bench angle on upper extremity muscular activation during bench press exercise
